nodes.v: The arrows are not integrations. All three write to the same Salesforce record directly.
Built natively on Salesforce, distributed on the AppExchange
Most commerce projects finish with two systems and an expensive sync between them.

The storefront goes on Shopify or WooCommerce. The customer record stays in Salesforce. Between them sits a connector, a nightly job and someone whose real job has quietly become reconciling orders. It holds together until it doesn't, and the first sign is usually a report that no longer matches the one beside it.

nodes.v: Automation that stops at the border
Salesforce cannot act on an abandoned cart, a stock hold or a warranty claim it never sees.
StoreConnect is an AppExchange package. The store runs inside Salesforce.

There is no API layer and no external database. Products, pricing, stock, orders, customers, pages and content are Salesforce records. Your admins already know how to change them, your reports already know where to find them, and your Flows can act on them the moment they are created.
Pages, blogs, navigation and media managed as Salesforce records, with full control of the theme, CSS and custom JavaScript. Media is served through a CDN.

nodes.v: Three situations where StoreConnect is the straightforward answer

You have Sales Cloud or Service Cloud and now need to sell online, or a storefront that never properly connected to either. StoreConnect puts commerce on the records you already trust, so pipeline, cases and orders finally sit together.

Shopify and BigCommerce will get you selling quickly. The cost turns up later, in integration work and a second set of customer data. If a single view of the customer matters more than a theme marketplace, that comparison is worth running properly. We will run it with you.

One-off and recurring donations, memberships, event tickets, merchandise and in-person sales, all against one supporter record. The account portal needs no Experience Cloud licences, which changes the sums considerably for a charity.
What an Enable StoreConnect build looks like
Each stage stands on its own. You can stop after the first one, and some organisations should.

Two weeks. We look at your catalogue, your selling model, the state of your Salesforce org and the systems StoreConnect would replace. You get a written recommendation with a real number attached, including the recommendation not to proceed where that is the right answer.

Data model, product and pricebook structure, stock, region-based tax, shipping and payment providers, and the Salesforce configuration commerce depends on. Delivered as a working store you can transact against, not a document describing one.

Theme, content, checkout, customer portal, and the register and hardware configuration for each site. Built to your brand rather than a template with your logo dropped into it. Where Agentforce is in scope, the commerce agent is grounded and evaluated here.

Training for the people who will run the store every day, full configuration and change documentation, and a support arrangement sized to what you actually need. The handover is written on the assumption you may never need to call us again.

Enable does not use lock-in contracts, non-competes or retainers. We believe in delivering a successful project: on budget, on time, and to the satisfaction of the customer. If we have done that, you will keep working with us because you want to.

StoreConnect charges a shared success fee on each transaction rather than a per-user licence, across three plan tiers that differ by storefront count, register count, hosting and support SLA. Volume drives the cost, not headcount, and the fee is capped per transaction. We size it with you before you commit to anything.

Fixed price, agreed before we start. We scope the work honestly and do it ourselves: no padded hours, no surprise invoices, and nothing on the bill you cannot point to. The fit assessment is priced separately and deliberately small, so you can stop after it without having bought a build.
These are StoreConnect platform customers, delivered across its global partner network.
Several legacy websites and servers replaced by one installation covering B2B, B2C, support referrals and admin.
Multiple merchandise stores across brands and currencies, with click and collect.
Course bookings, equipment sales and fundraising on one platform, with LMS integration.
A consumer storefront with the reporting and management back end built out in Salesforce.
Do we need Experience Cloud licences?
No. The customer account portal does not require them, and it works with SSO if you already run a portal of your own.
What happens to our ERP or accounting system?
It stays where it is. StoreConnect sits in Salesforce alongside the integrations you already have, and the StoreConnect ecosystem covers Xero, GoldFinch, NAO and others natively.
Can we keep our current website design?
Yes. The theme is fully adjustable, with custom CSS and JavaScript, so we rebuild the front end to your existing brand rather than asking you to accept a template.
How long does an implementation take?
A single storefront on a healthy Salesforce org is a matter of weeks. Multi-store, multi-currency or point of sale rollouts take longer. The fit assessment is where you get a real date.
Does it work properly in New Zealand?
Yes. Multi-currency and region-based tax are standard, several payment and shipping providers are supported, and local region hosting is available on the higher plans.
Tell us what you sell, and how.
A short conversation is usually enough to tell whether StoreConnect is the right answer for you. If it is not, we will say so, and point you at what is.
